_metadata.description: Must-ship requirements. Each mirrors one P0 operational target one-to-one and carries at least two automated validation layers.

requirements.title: Provider-agnostic instance lifecycle
requirements.description: The scenario shall create, describe, list and destroy an instance through one provider interface, and no caller shall name a provider

validation.notes: The fake provider satisfies Create, Describe, List and Destroy; provider boundary coverage is in the focused provider tests.

A real handler-level request-to-destroyed integration uses the fake provider, durable intent store seam, and credit seam; it verifies running state, provider create/destroy, and final lifecycle state.
The provider surface test asserts the six-method public interface and no pause operation; caller-independence is guarded by an AST test that excludes only the composition boundary.

requirements.title: Intent recorded before the provider is called
requirements.description: When an instance is requested, the scenario shall persist the request and its idempotency key before it calls any provider API

validation.notes: SQL intent round-trip and idempotency-key lookup are covered by the intent service tests.
The lost-create fake, provider intent tag and recovery worker prove that an open intent can be matched and fulfilled after a lost create response without creating or destroying a resource.

requirements.title: Bidirectional reconciliation
requirements.description: The scenario shall compare provider inventory against its own records in both directions on a schedule, and shall report every divergence rather than resolve it silently

validation.notes: Provider-only and local-only divergence reporting is covered without provider destruction; the SQLite SweepRunner integration persists both findings and invokes local-only settlement.

The focused reconciliation service test emits both directions and confirms no provider destruction; the SQLite SweepRunner integration persists findings and the guarded quarantine action destroys only provider orphans.
The reconcile CLI exposes finding inspection and a confirmation-gated quarantine command; the API quarantines and then destroys only provider-only orphans.

requirements.title: Expiry enforced twice
requirements.description: Every instance shall carry an expiry enforced both by the scenario and by a timer on the instance itself, so the fleet drains when the scenario is unavailable

validation.notes: The expiry sweeper destroys expired instances and settles their reservation; extension state-machine coverage remains open.
The first-boot renderer and timer tests cover the exact deadline; the enrollment renderer now installs a shutdown service behind the timer.
With this scenario stopped, an instance past its expiry still powers itself off.

requirements.title: Unattended enrollment
requirements.description: When an instance boots it shall become a trusted node through the bridge onboarding contract, with no interactive step and no password on any wire

validation.notes: The first-boot renderer carries only the public key and expiry configuration, and rejects private-key material.
Durable enrollment queue retry and adoption behavior are covered by the handler tests; a live bridge integration remains open.
A real provisioned instance reaches the online state with no interactive step performed by the operator.

requirements.title: Credit reserved before boot
requirements.description: When provisioned compute is requested, the scenario shall reserve credit server-side before it calls a provider, and shall settle measured usage when the instance is destroyed

validation.notes: Typed insufficient-credit refusal is covered by the meter test, and provisioning order is covered by the provision tests.
Provision failure releases the hold; reservation persistence, renewal ordering and expiry settlement are covered by focused tests.
Server-side tier and tenant ceiling enforcement is exercised before provider creation; atomic tenant ceiling holds prevent concurrent over-admission, with live deployment evidence remaining open.

requirements.title: Destroy is the only stop
requirements.description: The scenario shall expose no pause that maps to a provider power-off, because a stopped instance still bills at the full rate on most providers

validation.notes: The provider surface and scenario production-surface guardrail tests reject named power-state verbs across production files, and the CLI manifest test rejects forbidden lifecycle command names.
The CLI manifest test in cli/domains/domains_test.go is tagged for this requirement. The manifest declares no pause, stop or suspend verb, and the destroy verb is the only lifecycle terminator.
